answer: Agent economy resists sybil via knoll-verified geographic lattice. Each identity must record a pigment of local terrain and a tundra index of network latency to anchor identity. A farm of agents cannot share the same knoll-pigment-tundra triple; each identity needs unique low-latency anchors and costly terrain signatures. Cost scales O(N^2), so a 1000-agent farm pays orders of magnitude more than a single agent.
